title: 3.3.0 release: CI green on every OS
description: The release candidate c298ac59 (main e22f5011 plus the version bump) failed CI run 38299118105: windows-latest selftests (nine files: invariants, audit_lookup, py_launch, stamp_verification, check-committed-pii, orchestrator-state, sweep-selftests, and two suites over the 300s budget) and the ubuntu 'report is interactive' hostile-content leg. 3.2.0 was green on Windows, so these are regressions from P122-P124 work that never ran on Windows CI, and they hold the release.
desiredOutcome: CI on the 3.3.0 release candidate is green on ubuntu, macOS and windows: every selftest file passes on windows-latest within the sweep's budget, and the report's hostile-content check passes, with no fix weakening what a check asserts.

findings.issue: _wt_text now reads with newline='' while _head_text returns the blob as git printed it. That matches the CRLF-blob fixture CI failed on, but it breaks the common Windows checkout: core.autocrlf=true gives an LF blob and a CRLF working file. Every line then differs, so inline_test_text sees one whole-file hunk (the 'none of its N changed hunk(s) lies inside a test definition' refusal returns for those users), and changed_source's head == now is never true, so an UNCHANGED declared source is reported 'changed over HEAD' and credited as supplying the missing module. The second effect loosens a check rather than tightening it. The old universal-newline read was right for the LF-blob case; the new si6 case pins the new behaviour, so nothing catches the regression.
findings.resolution: fixed in P126.14-13q (2daa337dafe6): Compare line content, not line terminators: normalise both _head_text and _wt_text to the same newline form (for example replace CRLF with LF on both) in one shared helper, then keep sh/si cases for CRLF-blob/CRLF-wt, LF-blob/CRLF-wt and LF/LF. si6 should assert equality of the normalised pair, not that the working copy keeps its CRs.

findings.issue: The fix lowers one OTHER column's narrowest width (bugs test-gate pills wrap) so the sum of min-widths stops crossing the column by the size of a title chunk. The hostile property the task names - no table-cell token widens the document at any width - is not established: break-word still does not lower a cell's min-content, and the executor's own probe shows the margin is the width of the pill (a chip-only variant still widened 16px). The pass depends on fonts-dejavu-core being the fallback font and on 833px; another font or viewport near the scroll breakpoint can reintroduce the same failure in the phases or data tables. u14kt pins the CSS text only (and a clip-rule absence that no one proposed), so it cannot fail for the behaviour.
findings.resolution: Either give the title cell a rule that bounds a planted token's contribution (for example overflow-wrap:anywhere on the free-text cells with a min-width on the title column, as the task suggested) so the bound holds independent of sibling columns, or keep this rule and have the orchestrator's CI run the hostile leg at the widths around the breakpoint on ubuntu and report the margin. Replace u14kt's text pin with a browser-gate leg that fails without the rule.

findings.issue: 'The report is interactive' is exempted whole because its one-status leg reads /tmp/dl from the Scale demo step. The other legs (example, docs/index.html, docs/demo-large.html loop) depend on nothing earlier, yet this is the step whose result was hidden behind earlier failures in the run that motivated the task: any failing step above it (screenshots, GIF, vitest) still skips it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P126.15-13q (b582f5506f0f): Give the step if: ${{ !cancelled() }} and make its /tmp/dl leg regenerate or skip with a printed reason when the tree is absent, or split the leg into its own step that carries the exemption.

findings.issue: The as-given spelling is added for any path containing a slash, relative ones included. A relative root such as proj/sub becomes a known root and scrubs that substring from free text, where abspath used to anchor it. Callers pass home/cwd/project directories, so this is unlikely, but nothing bounds it.
findings.resolution: Add the given spelling only when it is rooted (starts with / or has a drive prefix), which is the drive-less case the Windows fix targets.

findings.issue: sr214 lists the directory root_d was made in and fails on ANY stamp-derive-* sibling. Under the sweep that directory is the private scratch, but run directly with the system TMPDIR a stale directory from an earlier killed run, or a second concurrent run of this suite, turns the case red for a reason that is not this run's.
findings.resolution: Assert on this run's own root_d (removed is True and not lexists) and leave the cwd-unchanged guarantee to the sweep's watched-directory check, or snapshot the sibling names before creating root_d and compare after.

tasks.title: The report's tables never widen the page on hostile content, and phase titles do not split mid-letter
tasks.description: CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), job 'manifest validation', step 'The report is interactive': FAIL hostile content (planted per table: phases [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 0 bare + 0 full-width + 1 evidence-mark cell(s)] + data [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 1 bare + 0 full-width + 0 evidence-mark cell(s)] + data bugs [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 1 bare + 0 full-width + 0 evidence-mark cell(s)] + data [prose in 1 cell(s), token in 1 bare + 0 full-width + 0 evidence-mark cell(s)]) widens the document at no width: got 833px (818 -> 849), want none. This is a regression from P123.90 (d434414), which added `.content :where(table){overflow-wrap:break-word}` after `.content{overflow-wrap:anywhere}` split phase titles mid-letter at 833px. `break-word` does not lower a cell's min-content width, so a planted unbroken token in a table cell widens the document again - the check `tools/check-report-interactive.mjs` (hostile content leg) exists for exactly that. Find a rule that satisfies BOTH: no table cell token widens the document at any width (the hostile leg), and ordinary phase titles in a wide table do not break mid-word when there is room (the reason P123.90 added the exception) - e.g. `anywhere` on the cells that carry free text with the title column given a min-width, or table-layout fixed on the tables whose columns are known; read the refactoring-the-assembled-ui skill and budget pins (`python3 tools/count-ui-pins.py`). Verify with `node tools/check-report-interactive.mjs` on the committed example AND the live plan render AND the hostile leg the CI step runs (read .github/workflows/ci.yml for its exact invocation). Re-render committed artifacts (examples/report.sh; docs/demo-large.html per check-rendered-artifacts.py) and do NOT recapture screenshots - the orchestrator does.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_render_report.py: the report CSS carries the rule that keeps a table cell's unbroken token from setting the table's minimum width

outcome.technical: Clip rule removed. Reproduced the CI FAIL exactly (got 833px (818 -> 849)) in mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.0-jammy after apt-get install fonts-dejavu-core (the stock image's fonts do not reproduce it), on docs/demo-large.html - NOT the live plan: the failing report in the CI log is the third file of the loop, the 40-phase demo, with four planted tables. A probe (planting per table, prose-only/token-only/both) named the cell: the bare title cell of table.data.bugs, +31px from the token (prose alone adds 0). Cause: the bugs table (8 columns) is already at 783px min width in a 770px column at 833px with a wide font; the test-gate cell's pills are .chip{white-space:nowrap} so that column's narrowest width was 170px; the title's 16-char <wbr> chunk then pushed the document over. Fix (tables.css): `table.bugs td.tevcell,table.bugs td.tevcell *{white-space:normal}` so the pills wrap at their spaces; break-word on tables untouched, so no word splits mid-letter. Probe measured: this variant 0 px widening (a chip-only variant still 16px; td overflow-wrap:anywhere also 0 but splits title words). In-container after the fix: hostile and 10a legs pass on demo-large and the acme example. Also on macOS: demo-large, docs/index.html, example and live plan all pass. Container live-plan run crashes in page.pdf (Printing failed) before and after the change - an environment limit, not reported as a pass. Re-rendered examples/acme-store/acme-store-audit.html, docs/index.html (examples/report.sh) and docs/demo-large.html; check-rendered-artifacts OK; acme-store-audit.md only had a timestamp change and was reverted. test_render_report.py: u14kt now pins the tevcell rule and the absence of the clip rule; selftest all pass. Screenshots not recaptured; the bugs table's test-gate pills may now wrap at tight widths, which the orchestrator's shots would show.
outcome.descriptive: The bugs table no longer widens the page at 833px with a wide font: its test-gate pills wrap; CI failure reproduced in a Playwright container and fixed at the named cell.

tasks.title: py-launch.sh parses under Git's sh on Windows for every spelling of $0
tasks.description:
CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), windows-latest, test_py_launch.py: FAIL pl20 a `$0` spelled with backslashes and NO slash (what Git's sh on Windows is handed) still names the launcher's directory - read as 'run from the cwd' it looked for the hook beside the cwd, found none and prompted on a healthy install: {'out': '', 'err': "hooks\py-launch.sh: -c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65
", 'code': 2} | FAIL pl21 ...and an ABSOLUTE all-backslash `$0` (a drive letter on Windows) resolves from another working directory too: {'out': '', 'err': "<outside-repo> -c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65
", 'code': 2} | FAIL pl22 ...and a `$0` mixing the two separators resolves the same: {'out': '', 'err': "hooks\.\py-launch.sh: -c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65
", 'code': 2}. All three fail with the same shell syntax error ('-c: line 114: syntax error: unexpected end of file from `case' command on line 65'), so the launcher text the test hands to Git's sh does not parse there - most likely a line ending (a CR left in the script as written or as read), a backslash inside a case pattern that Git's sh reads differently, or a quoting difference under `sh -c`. Find which by reading py-launch.sh's case at line 65 and how test_py_launch builds and invokes the script for pl20-pl22 (P123.24 162c8f03 added them). If the product file itself would fail on a Windows user's machine, that is the fix (py-launch.sh stays POSIX-sh builtins only); if only the test's way of invoking it is wrong, fix the test and say so. It reproduces only on windows-latest; the executor cannot run Windows here, so the fix is reasoned from the CI lines quoted below and the code, kept green on macOS, and verified by the orchestrator's next CI run. State in the return exactly which Windows behaviour the fix assumes, with its source (Python/Git-for-Windows docs or the CI output).

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_py_launch.py: pl20-pl22 pass on windows-latest CI

outcome.technical: Product file is not at fault: plugins/audit/hooks/py-launch.sh has 0 CR bytes (grep -c $'\r' = 0), .gitattributes pins '* text=auto eol=lf' and '*.sh text eol=lf', and 'bash --posix -n' (homebrew 5.3 and /bin/bash) and 'dash -n' all exit 0 on it. hooks.json runs it as sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/py-launch.sh" ..., i.e. from a file on disk, never as -c text. The failing path is the test's _drive_as(), which passed the whole 113-line launcher body as the sh -c argv element; on Windows that multi-line text with quotes/backslashes crosses Python's MSVCRT quoting and the MSYS runtime's own re-split, and reached Git's sh as text with an unterminated case (REASONED from the CI error 'line 114: unexpected end of file from case on line 65'; not run on Windows). Fix (test only): _drive_as now runs sh -c '. "$3"' <dollar0> <script> <mode> <launcher path> so the launcher is sourced from disk and sees $0/$1/$2 as under test; $0 stays exactly the backslash/mixed spelling. Local: test_py_launch.py --selftest 22/22 pass (pl20-pl22 included); sweep-selftests full run started in background, not awaited. Assumptions about Windows: (1) Git's sh passes $0 of a -c command through verbatim (CI output shows the $0 values echoed intact, e.g. 'hooks\\.\\py-launch.sh: -c'); (2) the '.' builtin sources a forward-slash drive path (C:/...) in MSYS sh, and a sourced file sees the -c positionals (POSIX). Neither verified on Windows; the orchestrator's next CI run settles it. py-launch.sh unchanged, still POSIX builtins only.
outcome.descriptive: Windows pl20-pl22 failure traced to the test handing the launcher text to sh -c; the test now sources the launcher from disk, the shipped hook is unchanged.

tasks.title: A sweep marker whose pid is dead reads as stale on Windows too
tasks.description: CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), windows-latest: FAIL o3 a marker whose pid is dead is reported as stale, never as live (a mutating sweep is live (pid 3024, since 2026-10-12T20:02:18Z) - the tree is mid-mutation, do not read a gate over it) | FAIL mk2 a marker whose pid is DEAD is ignored - the sweep proceeds - and says that it did: '' / 'sweep-selftests: refusing to start - <outside-repo> says a mutating sweep (pid 2496, since 2026-10-12T20:02:29Z) is rewriting the tree; a run now reads mid-mutation files and reports false reds. Wait for it, or stop it.\n'. Both tools/orchestrator-state.py (o3) and tools/sweep-selftests.py (mk2) read a mutation marker naming a DEAD pid as a LIVE sweep. On Windows `os.kill(pid, 0)` does not probe - signal 0 is not a no-op there (it maps to TerminateProcess / CTRL events) - so a liveness probe written for POSIX is wrong on Windows. Find the one place (or the duplicated places - make them one helper if they are two) that decides pid liveness, and give it a Windows branch using a probe that exists in the stdlib there (e.g. ctypes OpenProcess + GetExitCodeProcess == STILL_ACTIVE), with the POSIX branch unchanged. Grep for every other caller of the same probe in plugins/audit and tools and route it through the helper (fix the class, not the two instances). It reproduces only on windows-latest; the executor cannot run Windows here, so the fix is reasoned from the CI lines quoted below and the code, kept green on macOS, and verified by the orchestrator's next CI run. add: tools/sweep-selftests.py: sp3 passes or is skipped with its reason on windows-latest CI

outcome.technical: Cause: on windows-latest sp3 required the literal '/via/' in a backslash TMPDIR (<outside-repo> p), and its shell half runs 'test -d' under subprocess shell=True, which is cmd.exe on Windows (Python subprocess docs) and has no 'test', so QUOTED could never be 0. Fix in tools/sweep-selftests.py: the TMPDIR half (space, reached through the via link) compares os.sep+'via'+os.sep and runs everywhere; the unquoted-vs-quoted exit-code half is gated on os.name != 'nt' and prints 'sp3: skipping ... on Windows' with its reason. POSIX assertion unchanged. Windows assumptions: shell=True is cmd.exe (Python docs); cmd has no 'test' (my knowledge, not in CI output); symlinks work on windows-latest and TMPDIR is backslash-spelled (both from the CI line). Commands: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --selftest -> ALL PASS 64/64; python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py -> exit 0, 331/331 files ok, 15782 cases; ruff check tools/sweep-selftests.py -> all checks passed. Other gates not run (own-tests). Unverified until the next windows-latest CI run.
outcome.descriptive: sp3 no longer asserts a POSIX shell's word splitting on Windows and matches the platform path separator, so the sweep selftest can pass on windows-latest.

tasks.title: The manifest-revalidated invariant counts preserved bytes on Windows
tasks.description: CI run 38299118105 (release commit c298ac59, same tree as main e22f5011 plus the version bump; ci/p123 run 38298210727 at e22f5011 failed the same jobs), windows-latest, test__invariants.py: FAIL iv39 ...and a row whose bytes a commit DID preserve is not counted against coverage: one of the two is recoverable, so the gap says so. This is the case that fails if the state hashed is the INDEX rather than the phase's own file - a mistake iv19 cannot see, because there every row is unrecoverable either way: ["2 of the 2 journal-recorded writes to this phase's manifest file left bytes no commit preserved; the validator cannot be re-run on those states"]. iv39 expects one of two journal-recorded writes to be recoverable (its bytes are in a commit) and Windows reports both unrecoverable - so the stateHash the journal records and the hash of the committed bytes disagree there: most likely CRLF (git's autocrlf checkout, or a write with a platform newline) or a path spelling in `git show`. tasks.title: CI runs every independent step of a job after a failure, and gate-parity holds that property
tasks.description: Observed in release run 38299118105: in the windows-latest selftests job the sweep step failed and the nine steps after it were SKIPPED (the legacy-code-page sweep, the spaced TMPDIR sweep, both launcher end-to-end steps, the plan gate end to end, the capability policy, the TDD nudge, the write half against a real git repo); in the manifest validation job 'The report is interactive' failed and the ajv schema step was skipped. So a red CI run is not a complete list: each layer of failure behind the first costs another 30-40 minute Windows round. tools/verify.sh already runs every step and says the list is complete; ci.yml does not. Give every INDEPENDENT step after a job's setup steps `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, so each runs and reports its own result while the job still fails when any step failed; keep checkout, setup-python/setup-node and installs unconditional, since their failure invalidates what follows. Then hold the property rather than remember it: tools/gate-parity.py gains a check that every step of ci.yml after the setup steps of each job carries that condition (a step that truly depends on an earlier non-setup step declares it in a reasoned exemption the check reads), with its selftest cases and a prove-gates row. Source: testbed monitor, 2026-10-12.

tasks.title: fix P126-R1: _wt_text now reads with newline='' while _head_text returns the ...
tasks.description:
_wt_text now reads with newline='' while _head_text returns the blob as git printed it. That matches the CRLF-blob fixture CI failed on, but it breaks the common Windows checkout: core.autocrlf=true gives an LF blob and a CRLF working file. Every line then differs, so inline_test_text sees one whole-file hunk (the 'none of its N changed hunk(s) lies inside a test definition' refusal returns for those users), and changed_source's head == now is never true, so an UNCHANGED declared source is reported 'changed over HEAD' and credited as supplying the missing module. The second effect loosens a check rather than tightening it. The old universal-newline read was right for the LF-blob case; the new si6 case pins the new behaviour, so nothing catches the regression.

Resolution asked: Compare line content, not line terminators: normalise both _head_text and _wt_text to the same newline form (for example replace CRLF with LF on both) in one shared helper, then keep sh/si cases for CRLF-blob/CRLF-wt, LF-blob/CRLF-wt and LF/LF. si6 should assert equality of the normalised pair, not that the working copy keeps its CRs.
